findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed that PIC’s allergen certification is expired. PIC was aware that certification is expired, and will schedule to renew. Ensure compliance by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed raw chicken stored above raw beef in the walk-in cooler and prep cooler. These storage order violations were also observed in the previous spot check and last routine inspection. Informed PIC that raw beef must be stored above raw chicken due to the beef’s lower minimum cooking temperature. All storage order violations were corrected on site. A spot check will be conducted in the near future to ensure storage order guidelines are being followed. Ensure staff are educated on the proper order of storage for raw meats.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat 
Observed multiple items to be missing date marking (deli meats in prep cooler, cut vegetables and cooked meat in walk-in cooler). PIC was informed that any time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food stored in refrigeration for more than 24 hours needs to be properly date-marked and discarded after 7 days of retention. PIC placed labels on all required foods in prep cooler and walk-in during spot check. A follow-up will be conducted in 10 days (3/12/2025) to ensure that proper date marking is being followed.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:

The green beans were transferred to an appropriate vessel (metal pan) to complete its cooking. Violation is considered corrected on site.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an individual fail to use a barrier to turn off hand-sink faucet. Advised PIC to review proper handwashing with staff. A barrier must be used to turn off the faucet to prevent cross-contamination prior to handling food.

(C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following storage order violations:
1. Cooked turkey stored under raw beef in walk-in cooler
2. Cooked noodles stored under raw beef in walk-in cooler
3. Fish stored under raw chicken and raw beef in prep cooler
4. Raw hamburger stored over ready-to-eat feta cheese in prep cooler

The inspector will spot check for storage order during the scheduled follow-up.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed containers of cooked chicken and cooked meatloaf in walk-in-cooler to not have a date mark. Per PIC, items were prepared the previous day (6/19/24). Items were marked with proper date during inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. 

Containers of rice, cooked pasta in water and pancake batter are observed on shelves in the walk in cooler without covers. PIC instructed to ensure that all foods are protected from potential contamination while in storage. Lids were supplied to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The magnetic knife rack to the right of the prep cooler is observed heavily soiled. PIC instructed to clean often enough to protect the food contact surfaces of the utensils attached to it.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing. 

The shelves in the walk in cooler are observed soiled with thick accumulations of dust and rust. PIC instructed to clean them and maintain them clean. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

Multiple shelves in the walk in cooler next to the door to the walk in freezer are observed with rust. PIC instructed maintain smooth and easily cleanable. Painting the wire framing was suggested.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. The can opener blade and ice machine drop guard are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely so that soil does not accumulate. Blade was cleaned during the inspection to correct. 


4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. The nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed with a thick accumulation of slime. Situation was discussed with servers. One stated that the nozzles are cleaned every night. Another stated once a week. Inspector suggested that they are removed from the machine, disassembled and cleaned/ sanitized nightly so as to maintain clean. The nozzles were cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: 3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.  Both chicken and fish are observed in a sink in the kitchen area thawing without an approved method. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to thaw in an approved method.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: 6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. Multiple (approximately 5-6) flies are observed in the dish area of the facility. Another pair of flies were observed by the fountain drink machine in the server area. PIC is instructed to contact pest control and ensure effective methods are being used to combat pests in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Shelves found to be soiled in the walk in cooler of the establishment. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B). Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) Observed pans of raw beef stored above a tray of sliced deli ham. Store foods that do not require further washing or cooking above raw foods in order to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11. Ham was moved up above raw beef.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine registered 0ppm. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114. The bucket was replaced and the solution registered 100ppm. corrected on site
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The can opener blade and ice machine drop guard are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely so that soil does not accumulate.  Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on cheese cake, chololate pie, taco meat, pulled pork, hard cooked eggs in the wakin cooler and pie case. Potentially hazarduos ready to eat food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17. Foods were marked. Date mark foods and maintain a habit of properly date marking food.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at the wak in cooler. Observed foods to be uncovered such as taco meat, pulled pork and hard cooked eggs. Food shall be protected from contamination at all times. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Shelves found to be soiled in the walk in cooler of the establishment. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B). Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed the handle of the ladel in butter sauce to be wrapped with a towel. The towel was removed and discarede. 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of ladel handle not easily cleanable. Replace ladel with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 4-601.11  (C) Observed grease and soil accumulation present on the stove top and between the prep unit and the hot holding area. Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed crumbs and soil residue present on the shelves over and under hot holding area. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410. ILCS 625 Cec. 3.07 - Allergen training required for this facility.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: Observed soup to be sitting on the side area at 97F. Soup was discarded in the garbage. Observed two pans of Lasagna to be sitting on the side area at 75F and 95F. The Lasagna is said to have been removed from the oven around 12 o'clock noon. The Lasagna was immediately placed into the oven to reheat to 165F. Cool foods properly. 750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed the cutting boards to have been scored from use. The scores have some soil accumulation. Clean and maintain cutting surfaces free of scores.  Sand the cutting boards so that the scores are removed and can not hold soil. 750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Observed link sausage and soup to be cooling in the walk in cooler with no time on the label. Provide proper date and time tags to cooling foods. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed gilled onions in the bottom of the prep cooler with no date marking, Observed cream pies and cheese cake in the facility with no date marking. Make sure to mark all food that is potentially hazardous foods that are ready to eat and use or discard in 7 days. Pies and onions were date marked. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
repeat

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment: Observed cooked bacon to be placed on a towel that is on the prep table cutting board. The towel had previously held shell eggs and had a bowl used for scrambling raw eggs next to it. Grease from the bacon was then dabbed off with a towel that is hanging on the belt of the cook. The order of bacon was discarded and a fresh order was cooked. The towel was also removed from the counter. Discontinue this practice. 750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed employee to wash hands and then push the faucet handle back down with his thumb. The employee also used the towel hanging on his belt to dry his hands. The employee was coached immediately on proper hand washing and drying practices. 750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.
750-530e Employees shall maintain a high degree of personal cleanliness and shall conform to good hygienic practices during all working periods in the food service establishment.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Observed the dish machine to have 0ppm of chlorine upon arrival. The machine was primed and tested again. The machine now tests with 50 ppm of residual chlorine. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration. Keep a log and test the machine at least once per day. Once per shift would be best practice.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following items to be soiled with crumbs and food debris: 1) bottom shelf next to shells (corn silks) 2) top of hot holding 3) door handles of upright freezer 4) white slotted shelves in the prep cooler. Clean and maintain clean. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: Upon arrival there are no hand towels at the hand sink. Keep the hand sink supplied with hand towels. Towels were provided. 750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Ham, pies (except fruit pies) and turkey in the walk in cooler are observed to be missing 7 day date marks. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: Observed soup cooling on the pickle bucket for two hours to be at 118F.  The soup was heated to 165F and placed on the hot holding.  Cool foods properly or hot hold.  Do not allow foods to move into the temperature danger zone without active supervision. 750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: Pie case is reading 48F air temperature. The pies that are cream pie, pumpkin, or meringue were discarded. The fruit pies will be kept and have been moved to the walk in cooler.  750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed a ladles in the clean utensil tub to have food soil on it. Also, Observed can opener to have some paper soil on it. Clean food contact surfaces and maintain clean. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed clean utensils to be in a plastic tub which is soiled in the bottom with crumbs. Clean the tub and  utensils and maintain  free of crumbs and dust. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Observed the noodles cooling with no time for cooling. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Properly time mark cooling items.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed eggs and link sausage in the prep top to be 50F and 45F internally. Do not leave the prep top open when not in use. Also, fewer eggs can be stored in the top to allow for eggs to be a proper temperature. A riser in the bottom of the pan can stop eggs from touching the bottom o f the pan which may help with freezing. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
Items that are cooked and ready to eat are not date marked in the cooler including turkey, ham, and sausage. Make sure to use the 7 day date marking rule on all foods that are ready to eat and potentially hazardous. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: Observed chickens and turkeys in the prep sink with not in water but with running water. Sink was plugged so that water would collect and water was left running. 750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Observed the chicken to be over pork in the reach in prep cooler bottom. The foods were re arranged to store properly. 750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: There are several pieces of equipment that are no longer operational and should be removed from the facility. At a minimum keep equipment for sale clean and uncluttered. 750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment: Discussed complaint with owner. He states that a lady came to him and asked to make pies for the restaurant from her home kitchen. The owner agreed and said that he did not know this practice was not allowed. He stated that when they opened the got pies from a wholesale company and will return to buying the pies from that company. 750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited. The pies were discarded in the garbage.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed no date marking on the milk or juice in the wait cooler nor on the ham cubes in the walk in cooler. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. Properly date mark items.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: Upon arrival a bin of frozen chicken is observed to be sitting on the floor to the right of the walk in cooler door. The chicken is frozen and the manager tells me that he knows it should be in running water to thaw.  The chicken was placed into multiple smaller containers and placed under running water to thaw. 750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Observed the bin of frozen chicken on the floor. The chicken was placed into proper containers, moved up off of the floor and some thawing was started. 750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed a scoop to be ready for use in the ice cream to be stored in a container of water which is 75F. Discard water container and store scoop properly.  Scoop can also be stored hot held. 750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: There is no sanitizer in the bucket hooked up to the dish machine. The chemical sanitizer residual is 0ppm.  750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration. The bucket of sanitizer was replaced. Now there is proper chemical sanitizer going to the dish machine.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the soda nozzels to be soiled. Also, the fire supression lines over the grill have some soil (frease and dust) accumulated. Properly clean these areas so that soil does not accumulate. Suggest using a brush for soda nozzels so that mold does not accumulate in the aeration section. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The microwave is soiled on the inside and outside. Clean and maintain clean. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed the white bucket holding steak knives to be soiled with dust and food debris in the bottom. Properly clean bucket and knives. Put bucket on regular cleaning schedule. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Pancake batter is reconstituted and placed in the cooler with no date tag. 750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. Properly date mark all foods.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed shell eggs in the cooler prep top with an internal temperature of between 45F and 55F. Eggs were discarded in the garbage. 750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service. Do not stock eggs so high in the prep top. Suggest placing ice on shell eggs and keeping a smaller amount in the top pans.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: At 11:15am extra soup at 108F is observe in the walk in cooler in a container deeper than 4 inches with no date or time mark. According to the owner the soup was placed into the cooler at 9:30am. The soup was moved to a shallow metal pan and placed in to the walk in freezer to continue cooling. 750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. Discussed other options for extra soup that do not include cooling and reheating until it is known if the soup will be utilized that day.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed ice scoop in  ice bin with handle in contact with the ice. 750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. Store scoop properly. Ice scoop was removed from ice.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed soup spoons at the salad bar to have eating surfaces exposed. 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Properly protect the eating surfaces of utensils. Plastic wrap was used to protect eating surfaces. Suggest using a holder to present the handles of the spoons to customers.
